body.estimand_functional: Put \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}\) and let \(b_n=n^{-2t/(4t+d)}\) for \(d\leq4t\), while \(b_n=n^{-4t/(4t+3d)}\) for \(d>4t\).  The proved all-regime statement is \(c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  On the proved no-penalty subregion \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\), \(\rho_n^*\asymp\rho_{n,e}^*\asymp n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\), with no logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\).  No independently derived repaired lower and upper maps have yet been proved equivalent.  The complete all-regime frontier, its unresolved transition logarithms, and the necessary direction of the known-propensity comparison therefore remain open; no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

sampling_model.design: Project-specific strengthening: \(X\) is known to be exactly uniform on the entire cube \([0,1]^d\), not merely to have a bounded density or to be uniform on a support with holes.
sampling_model.units: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed observed margins of a law in \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary \(A\) has unknown propensity \(e\) under the observational experiment; the comparison experiment supplies the exact function \(e_P\) to the test.
sampling_model.outcome: Observed and potential outcomes are binary.  The pointwise boxes \(m_0,m_1\in[1/4,3/4]\) are project-specific fixed interior regression margins on the canonical continuous representatives.
sampling_model.overlap: The project-specific numerical overlap box is \(e(x)\in[1/4,3/4]\) for every \(x\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance estimator and no nuisance convergence rate is part of the class; all tuning is a deterministic function of \(n,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a pointwise CATE-estimation minimax rate in a larger model with a merely bounded covariate density and real outcomes; Section 3.1 supplies localized fuzzy-hypothesis and Hellinger machinery.  Its binary lower submodel uses a density uniform on an \(n\)-dependent support-with-holes \(S_{h,k}\), so that lower bound does not transfer downward to the present exact full-cube uniform-design subclass.
Theorems 4 and 6 give fixed-alternative consistency and a local weak limit for quantitative homogeneity tests over structured rule classes under the paper's nuisance conditions.

Theorems 1--2 establish asymptotic normality for propensity-reweighted pairwise and multisample adjusted \(U\)-statistics under consistent propensity estimation, independent stratum samples, stable positive sample fractions, and pointwise overlap.

Section 3 derives joint asymptotic normality and Gaussian-simulation calibration for multisample \(U\)-statistics testing equality of additive treatment effects across a fixed collection of mutually independent prespecified strata.

Theorem 6 gives asymptotic level, fixed-alternative consistency, and nontrivial \(n^{-1/2}\)-local power for a multiplier-bootstrap test of homogeneous restricted CATE with possibly right-censored duration outcomes.

Section 4 gives a conservative finite-sample-valid Fisher randomization test for the sharp null of one unknown constant individual treatment effect by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over a confidence set for that nuisance effect.

The main martingale-transformation results give asymptotic level for a permutation test of a constant marginal-distribution shift with an estimated nuisance shift, retaining exact level only for the more restrictive sharp null.
Theorems 3 and 7 give asymptotic chi-square tests of equality of finitely many score-defined group average treatment effects under complete randomization, with sample splitting or cross-fitting.

Theorems 4.1 and 5.2 give matching nonasymptotic binned conditional-independence radii for fixed discrete responses and a continuous conditioner under total-variation smoothness, a different null manifold and separation metric from constant CATE.

Theorems 6 and 7 give null validity and spline minimax power for projected conditional covariance under common smoothness and nondegeneracy restrictions, rather than a fixed-sample three-smoothness CATE radius.

Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 characterize bias, variance, and optimal separate wavelet resolutions for estimation of a signed expected conditional covariance functional; they guide nuisance resolution but do not test an unknown constant CATE.
The main minimax theorems derive sharp heteroskedasticity-detection rates using a squared first-difference proxy under a rough unknown mean.
Theorem 1 gives asymptotic normality and type-I error control for an intra-fold split CATE-variance statistic under explicit nuisance learner-rate conditions.
The paper proves that the propensity score is ancillary for semiparametrically efficient estimation of the regular average treatment effect under ignorability.
Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 give asymptotic null validity and consistency against smooth local sieve alternatives for the null that the conditional average treatment effect is constant.

The paper develops \(L_1\)-type tests based on uniformly consistent nonparametric kernel estimators for conditional treatment-effect restrictions and proves asymptotically correct size, fixed-alternative consistency, and power against some local alternatives.
Section 1 records the classical nonadaptive Hölder goodness-of-fit boundary, and the paper establishes the iterated-logarithmic price of adaptation in wavelet testing.

body.tldr: Let \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  The observational radius satisfies the proved all-regime upper bound \(\rho_n^*\le Cb_n\) and, for \(d\ge2s_0\), the original fixed-sample lower bound \(\rho_n^*\ge c\max\{n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\}\), with no logarithm at \(d=2s_0\).  The no-penalty region \(s_0\ge\gamma\), \(d\le4\gamma\) remains matched.  A strict penalty is now proved whenever \(\gamma>s_0\) and \(d>2s_0\gamma/(\gamma-s_0)\): then \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\ge c n^{2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\to\infty\).  At \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), the exponent is at least \(4/35\).  The complete frontier and its remaining transition boundaries are open; no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Published CATE-homogeneity procedures and adjacent minimax results do not give the fixed-sample critical radius or the exact value-of-known-propensity frontier on this binary exact-uniform class.  The direct-Hellinger construction determines a nuisance-driven converse for \(d\ge2(\alpha+\beta)\), and comparison with the known-propensity benchmark proves strict divergence when \(\gamma>\alpha+\beta\) and \(d>2(\alpha+\beta)\gamma/(\gamma-\alpha-\beta)\).  The best proved observational upper map still does not match the converse outside the no-penalty region, so necessity and the transition boundaries remain unresolved.
project_justification.niche: The live niche is the interaction among a composite unknown-constant CATE null, separately rough propensity and baseline functions, exact full-cube design, and connected repeated-cell collisions.  An attaining test must use an omnibus population functional richer than both a within-bin covariance factor and the algebraically equivalent residual of a projected four-cell law.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies an explicit total profiled fourth-order test and all-regime upper bound, the known-propensity benchmark and matched no-penalty region, and a same-class fixed-\(n\) lower construction giving \(n^{-2(\alpha+\beta)/(2(\alpha+\beta)+d)}\) whenever \(d\ge2(\alpha+\beta)\).  Combining that converse with the known-propensity benchmark yields the explicit polynomial lower bound \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\ge c n^{2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)-2(\alpha+\beta)/(2(\alpha+\beta)+d)}\) throughout the proved strict-penalty region, without claiming that this sufficient region is necessary or that the complete frontier is solved.

body.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 remains a method donor rather than the source of the present class: its pointwise-estimation model is larger and its binary lower submodel uses a support with holes.  The converse here uses the localized fuzzy-hypothesis idea only after proving exact full-cube uniform masses, componentwise binary margins, a common sign-conditioned singleton predictive law, and a bounded-overlap connected-graph Hellinger calculation.  NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 gives collision-sensitive conditional-independence testing under a different null and metric; LundborgKimShahSamworth2024, corresponding to PCM arXiv:2211.02039, gives projected-covariance validity and spline power under common-smoothness conditions; DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026, arXiv:2410.00985v4, gives asymptotic structured-rule homogeneity results under nuisance conditions; and McGrathMukherjee2026, arXiv:2212.14857v5, derives separate resolutions for estimating a signed expected conditional covariance.  None supplies the componentwise constant-null fixed-sample nuisance lower map proved here, the resulting explicit sufficient strict-divergence region for unknown versus known propensity, or an omnibus test that closes the remaining same-class frontier.
body.technical_internal_limitation: With \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\), the optimized lower construction takes \(h\asymp\delta^{1/s_0}\), \(H\asymp\max\{h,\delta^{1/\gamma}\}\), \(q_e=2\delta^{\alpha/s_0}\), and \(q_b=2\delta^{\beta/s_0}\).  Its sign-conditioned connected-graph bound yields \(H^2\le Cn^2h^d\delta^2\sum_{k\ge2}(Cnh^d)^{k-2}\), which closes for \(d\ge2s_0\) and not at the natural scale for \(d<2s_0\).  For the bounded richer-upper attempt, the projected full-cell residual obeys the exact identity \(r_B(c)=\operatorname{Cov}(A,Y\mid B)-c\operatorname{Var}(A\mid B)\).  At the stress tuple the legal masking alternative has \(r_B(1/8)=0\) in every fine cell at \(h\asymp\delta^5\), even though \(\|e(1-e)(\tau-1/8)\|_2\gtrsim\delta\).  Hence every tensor unbiased for squared coefficients of that projected residual has zero population target at \(\delta\asymp n^{-2/7}\); the attempt stops before Hoeffding calibration.  A different population functional and the dense-regime converse remain necessary.
body.honest_scope: The causal estimand and statistical class remain unchanged: binary outcomes, exact uniform design on the full cube, fixed overlap and interior margins, three fixed Hölder indices, and an unknown constant null.  No nuisance-rate, learner, or estimator-side condition was added.  The proved content is an all-regime bracket, a matched sufficient no-penalty region, the sparse-regime nuisance converse, and an architecture-specific projected four-cell collapse diagnostic.  At the rough stress tuple the exponents remain \(2/7\) and \(4/19\), so the frontier is not claimed sharp.  The strict known-versus-unknown region is sufficient, not necessary; dense-regime lower optimization, a different omnibus upper construction, and unresolved transition logarithms remain open.  No result certifies an existing causal forest, and non-rejection is not evidence of homogeneity.
body.interpretation: In sparse rough-nuisance regimes, repeated-cell scarcity creates a detectability cost without positing a nuisance estimator.  At \((1,1,1/10,1/10)\), heterogeneity below order \(n^{-2/7}\) cannot be uniformly detected when the propensity is unknown, whereas supplying it permits order \(n^{-2/5}\); the radius ratio grows at least as \(n^{4/35}\).  The projected four-cell failure says only that one natural omnibus construction has no population signal on the masking witness.  These are worst-case experiment benchmarks, not validation of a fitted forest and not a license to interpret non-rejection as constant treatment effect.
